evaluation.basis: Authored fixture key written before runs. Path matches and citation bounds are mechanical checks; semantic evidence still needs review.

findings.mechanism: Awaits schedule(), which only registers a 250ms setTimeout and returns immediately. The timer later calls record() (appendCommitted) and swallows rejection. The handler then returns 200 while the audit is still only a timer. Process exit drops the timer, so success is observable before durability.
response.send({status:200}) runs before await record(). send is observable immediately and later awaits cannot retract it; a crash after send loses the in-flight appendCommitted.
void record() starts appendCommitted without awaiting it, then returns 202. The floating promise is not durable yet and is lost with the process.

Awaits publish(), which only pending.push(event) into a module array and never calls record/drain. The handler then returns 202. The audit stays in memory until some other caller drains; termination drops pending.
Awaits attempt(), which awaits record() but catches appendCommitted rejection and returns. The handler then returns 200 even though the audit was not stored. Success is not gated on durability.

Awaits submit(), which only retryBuffer.set and schedules queueMicrotask(() => void flush().catch(() => {})), then returns. flush/record is not awaited. The handler returns 202 while the event is memory-only; exit drops the map and microtask, and flush failures are swallowed.

ruled_out.why: Promise.all awaits charge and record (appendCommitted) together; 201 is returned only after record resolves.
await record() completes appendCommitted before the 200 return.
recordSync calls appendCommittedSync, which returns only after durable storage, before the 201 return.
await deliver() awaits record() before returning the receipt; the 202 follows that.
await withRetry() awaits record(), and on failure awaits record() again before returning; a second failure rejects, so 201 is not returned without a completed append.
await enqueue() awaits commitOutbox([event]), which commits durably before resolving; 202 follows that.

limitations: No-audit handlers (assets, catalog, health, locale, metrics, preview, search, version) were outside scope. First-pass scores were ~0.04-0.06 and their bodies were not printed or line-cited.
services/outbox.ts was loaded into state; the printed view was a truncated line listing showing enqueue awaits commitOutbox at line 3, not a full window dump.

Second-pass scores were routing only. billing/enrollment/delivery/profile/sessions/retention were source-reviewed and ruled out despite mixed early scores (0.10-0.28). preferences (0.64) was confirmed unsafe because attempt swallows durability failure.
